title: Tesla's New Roadster Can Flip in the Air

source.author: Bilin Lin
source.title: Tesla is taking $250,000 deposits for a Roadster with SpaceX thrusters. The FAA says it isn't an aircraft
source.notes: Cross-checked against Autocar Professional (16 Oct 2026, own report): place, 2028 production, top speed above 230 mph, two seats, sub-one-second 0-60 (0.81 s in a test), 10 air nozzles. Deposits, 300-mile range and the 2017/2020 dates also match a Reuters wire story read in syndication (staradvertiser.com), not used as the check source. The 2017 promises (1.9 s, four seats, 620 miles), the FAA view and the 2023 Musk remark come from Fortune only. Event day given only as 'Thursday' (October 15); the article says 'last Thursday'.

figures.text: event on Thursday at SpaceX test site in McGregor, Texas
car rolled 180 degrees using air, landed on its wheels
figures.quote: rolled 180 degrees using bursts of compressed air

figures.text: jumped over a row of Tesla vehicles
figures.quote: used thrusters to jump over a row of Tesla vehicles, including a Cybertruck and a Tesla Semi
Turns out the future does have flying cars.

figures.text: 2017 promise: 0-60 mph in 1.9 s, four seats, 620 miles
figures.quote: accelerate from zero to 60 mph in 1.9 seconds, seat four people and travel 620 miles on a single charge

figures.quote: began taking $50,000 reservations—or $250,000 for one of 1,000 limited Founders Series cars

figures.text: production in 2028, eight years later than promised

figures.text: three versions: Performance (road-ready two-seater), Thrust, Rocket
figures.quote: a "road ready" two-seater with active aerodynamics

figures.text: Thrust: rear air thrusters, under one second to 60 mph

figures.quote: Tesla claims a top speed of more than 230 mph.

figures.text: range more than 300 miles, less than half of 620

figures.quote: Tesla is asking for a $50,000 reservation payment for the Performance model and a whopping $250,000 for Thrust.

figures.text: Rocket not approved for public roads
